title: Trust Hinders Bidirectional Human-AI Alignment
abstract: arXiv:2610.15136v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Trust calibration remains the dominant framing of AI-assisted decision making: the goal is to close the gap between perceived and actual trustworthiness of AI systems so that users exhibit appropriate reliance on them. We argue that this approach, while useful for decision problems that are well-defined and clearly scoped, overly restricts what it means to make a decision with AI support. To overcome this limitation, we develop three dimensions of AI-assisted decision making. First, trusting AI is only one of several possible strategies for managing uncertainty. Second, trust calibration is often misapplied when AI models "large-world" decision problems, i.e., ill-defined situations where goals and states are only partially known or unknowable. Third, in such settings human-AI alignment requires addressing higher-order decision processes. We conclude by reflecting on the implications of our observations on the design of process-oriented

translated_title: 信任阻碍双向的人机对齐
translated_abstract: 信任校准仍然是AI辅助决策领域的主导框架：其目标是弥合AI系统感知可信度与实际可信度之间的差距，从而使用户对AI表现出适当的依赖。我们认为，这种方法虽然适用于定义明确、范围清晰的决策问题，但过度限制了“在AI支持下进行决策”的含义。为了克服这一局限性，我们提出了AI辅助决策的三个维度。第一，信任AI只是管理不确定性的几种可能策略之一。第二，当AI为“大世界”决策问题建模时，信任校准往往被误用，即那些目标和状态仅部分已知或不可知的定义模糊的情境。第三，在这种情境下，人机对齐需要处理更高阶的决策过程。最后，我们反思了这些观察对面向过程的设计所带来的启示。
tldr: 本文指出信任校准框架过度限制了AI辅助决策的理解，提出信任只是管理不确定性的策略之一，并论证在“大世界”决策问题中，人机对齐需要转向处理更高阶的决策过程。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that the trust calibration framework overly restricts AI-assisted decision making, proposing that trusting AI is merely one of several uncertainty management strategies, and that human-AI alignment in "large-world" decision problems requires addressing higher-order decision processes.
